{{Short description|Australian scientist and chemical engineer}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=April 2022}}
'''István Tóth''' is an [[Australians|Australian]] [[scientist]] and [[chemical engineer]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Oral hookworm vaccine could save millions around the world |url=https://www.uq.edu.au/news/article/2021/10/oral-hookworm-vaccine-could-save-millions-around-world-0 |website=UQ News| access-date=27 December 2021|language=en}}</ref> He is the Chair of Biological Chemistry and Professor of Pharmacy at the [[University of Queensland]].

== Education ==
Has a Master's in Chemical Engineering and a Ph.D. from the [[Technical University of Budapest|Technical University Budapest]] and is a member of the [[Hungarian Academy of Sciences]]. Toth is also a fellow of the Queensland Academy of Art and Sciences and [[Royal Australian Chemical Institute]], and Affiliated Professorial Research Fellow and Group Leader at Institute of Molecular Biosciences, UQ.

== Career ==
After earning his Ph.D., he spent two years at [[Carleton University]], Ottawa. In 1977, Toth returned to [[Budapest]] and began working at the Central Research Institute for Chemistry of the Hungarian Academy of Sciences before relocating to the [[School of Pharmacy, University of London|School of Pharmacy University of London]] in 1987.

In 1994, Toth was awarded a DSc degree by the Hungarian Academy of Sciences for his work on drug delivery. He then joined the University of Queensland in 1998 to lead a productive medicinal chemistry research group<ref>{{cite web |title=Professor Istvan Toth |url=https://scmb.uq.edu.au/profile/105/istvan-toth |website=University of Queensland |language=en |date=20 December 2021|access-date=27 December 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Hungarian Scientist Leads Development of Anti-Parasitic Vaccine |url=https://hungarytoday.hu/hookworm-vaccine-hungarian-scientist/ |website=Hungary Today |language=en |date=7 November 2021|access-date=27 December 2021}}</ref> and became an Australian citizen in the year 2000.

Toth is an elected Fellow of the [[Royal Australian Chemical Institute]], Fellow of the Queensland Academy of Arts and Sciences and Member (External) of the [[Hungarian Academy of Sciences]].

In 2009, he received the Adrian Albert award for sustained research in medicinal biochemistry. In 2019, he received the Doctor Honoris Causa Degree by the [[Semmelweis University]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Honorary doctors and PhD doctors conferred at closing event of international research week |url=https://semmelweis.hu/english/2019/11/honorary-doctors-and-phd-doctors-conferred-at-closing-event-of-international-research-week/ |website=Semmelweis University|access-date=27 December 2021}}</ref>
